title: Coherent finite reduction model for completed coefficient extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. On $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $A_m=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m)_W$, $B_m=(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m)_W$, $R_E=\varprojlim A_m$, and $R_L=\varprojlim B_m$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. The coefficient maps $A_m\to B_m$ and $R_E\to B_m$ are those of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], with actual quotient transitions. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_E))$ let $K_m=K\otimes^L_{R_E}A_m$ and let $S_{E,L}K$ be the completed scalar extension of that definition, computed on one flat-term K-flat representative $P$ by $R\lim_m\operatorname{Res}^L_m(P\otimes_{R_E}B_m)$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

The system $C_{E,L}(K)_m=K_m\otimes^L_{A_m}B_m$, with transitions from the actual quotient maps, is normalized [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. There is a natural isomorphism of coherent derived $B_\bullet$-systems
$$\mathcal R_L(S_{E,L}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{E,L}(K),$$
where $\mathcal R_L$ is derived reduction with its coherent quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. This map is the coherent counit [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] for the normalized system represented by $(P\otimes_{R_E}B_m)_m$, followed by the inverse of the simultaneous scalar-association isomorphisms
$$(P\otimes_{R_E}A_m)\otimes_{A_m}B_m\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_{R_E}B_m,\quad(x\otimes a)\otimes b\longmapsto x\otimes ab.$$
It is independent of the representative through the canonical resolution comparisons and is compatible with every transition $B_m\to B_n$. For $L=E$ it is the usual reduction counit. For $E\subset L\subset F$ the same comparisons agree under successive extension with the comparison for $E\subset F$, using the scalar-association maps, as an identity of coherent quotient-system comparisons. No unramifiedness, flatness of $A_m\to B_m$, boundedness or constructibility of $K$ is assumed.

source.place: Integral operations and common-stage scalar-extension clauses, with the actual quotient construction in def-weil-integral-scalar-extension; explicit coherent reduction refinement supplied by the agent.

proof.text: The finite quotient sheaf maps commute with transitions: apply faithfulness of forgetting commutativity, functoriality of constant sheafification, and integralScalarQuotientMap_transition to the ULift-transported ring maps. A private ring-level calculation within the same module handles the ULift representatives. This proves coefficientExtensionQuotient_naturality; the following steps record the proved identity clause and the plans for the two remaining main theorem holes.

Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Set $P_m=P\otimes_{R_E}A_m$ and $D_m=P\otimes_{R_E}B_m$, with the actual quotient maps on the coefficient factor. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], both are flat-term K-flat over their respective finite coefficient sheaves. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $P_m$ computes $K_m$, and $P_m\otimes_{A_m}B_m$ computes $C_{E,L}(K)_m$. The same lemma applies to $D_m\otimes_{B_m}B_n$ and, later, to extension from $B_m$ to a third coefficient quotient. All these are applications to morphisms of sheaves of rings on the same site, so no flatness of any coefficient homomorphism is required.

Define $a_m:P_m\otimes_{A_m}B_m\to D_m$ by $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes\iota_m(a)b$. Its inverse is $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b$. The balancing relations for $R_E\to A_m\to B_m$ make both maps well-defined and their composites identities. These formulas on sectionwise tensors induce the sheaf maps of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; extending over either sheafified factor is justified by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension]. They commute with the differentials since coefficients have degree zero. For $m\geq n$, either route through the quotient-transition square sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes\iota_n(q^A_{m,n}(a))q^B_{m,n}(b)$: this equals $x\otimes q^B_{m,n}(\iota_m(a)b)$ by [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Thus $a_\bullet$ is an isomorphism of strict quotient systems, not just a family of isomorphisms in the level categories.

source.place: Integral operations clause: simultaneous scalar association on the actual quotient models; agent supplies the formulas

proof.text:
Read $D_\bullet$ as a strict tower of $R_L$-complexes through the maps $R_L\to B_m$ of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. It therefore supplies the coherent tower datum required by [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. For $m\geq n$, K-flatness from [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] compute the normalization comparison by
$$(P\otimes_{R_E}B_m)\otimes_{B_m}B_n\longrightarrow P\otimes_{R_E}B_n,\qquad(x\otimes b)\otimes c\longmapsto x\otimes q^B_{m,n}(b)c.$$
Its inverse is $x\otimes c\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes c$, using exactly the balancing argument of step 2. The adjoint of this map is $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes q^B_{m,n}(b)$, the specified transition. For $r\geq m\geq n$, the two composites take $x\otimes b$ to $x\otimes q^B_{r,n}(b)$, and $q^B_{n,n}=1$. This proves normalization and its cocycle. The strict isomorphism $a_\bullet$ of step 2 transports these properties to $C_{E,L}(K)$ with its stated transitions.

source.place: Integral operations clause: normalization of the coefficient-extension quotient system

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal L_LD=R\lim_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mD_m$. By [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension, lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined] this is $S_{E,L}K$, with the same limit projections. The functors $\mathcal R_L\dashv\mathcal L_L$ and their counit in the derived system category are those of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] to the normalized tower of step 3, using coefficient field $L$. Its coherent counit is an isomorphism $e_D:\mathcal R_L\mathcal L_LD\xrightarrow{\sim}D$. Consequently
$$\phi_{E,L,K}=a_\bullet^{-1}e_D:\mathcal R_L(S_{E,L}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{E,L}(K).$$
The reduction tower here is the one of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Coherence of $e_D$ and strict transition compatibility of $a_\bullet$ prove compatibility of $\phi$ with every quotient $B_m\to B_n$. Effectivity assumes neither boundedness nor constructibility, so this applies to the arbitrary $K$ in the statement.

source.place: Canonical coherent counit isomorphisms for every normalized DVR tower

proof.text: For a chain map $u:P\to P'$, the maps in steps 2 and 3 commute with $u\otimes1$ on every quotient: both composites send $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $u(x)\otimes\iota_m(a)b$. The derived-system adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] makes its counit natural for the induced system morphism; its evaluations are adjoint to the limit projections. Thus $\phi$ is natural on flat-term K-flat representatives. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], a quasi-isomorphism of such representatives induces quasi-isomorphisms on all their quotient models; by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined] it also induces the canonical isomorphism on the completed extension. The equivalence $W_{R_E}^{-1}\mathcal P_{R_E}\simeq D(R_E)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] now descends this naturality: invert the arrows of a roof, and the same commuting square holds because its vertical arrows are isomorphisms. This proves naturality for arbitrary derived morphisms and independence under the canonical resolution comparisons, including their composition for a third representative.

source.place: Integral operations clause: independence of K-flat representatives and naturality; agent supplies the localization argument

proof.text: For identity coefficients, prove the actual finite quotient maps are identities by quotient induction and functorial constant sheafification. The sectionwise specification of systemMap then makes the sequence ring map the identity. Restriction along identity is naturally isomorphic to identity on module sheaves. Transport the ordinary scalar adjunction along this restriction unitor; uniqueness of left adjoints gives the ordinary scalar unitor. Its unit equation and the specified unit_section give the formula a tensor x maps to a times x. Apply uniqueness of left derived functors to this ordinary unitor; the universal counit factorization supplies precisely the required model equation, for every complex (in particular every K-flat one). Whisker this unitor by SE.reduction. Expanding the specified comparison gives reduction of the inverse completion followed by the reduction/limit counit. Its naturality proves coefficientExtensionReduction_identity. No effectivity theorem or completeness of K is used for this identity clause.

source.place: Identity coefficient extension and the reduction counit

proof.text:
For $E\subset L\subset F$, put $T_m=(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m)_W$. Its maps $A_m\to B_m\to T_m$ compose to the direct $A_m\to T_m$, by the inclusions and quotients of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Write $M=\mathcal L_LD=S_{E,L}K$ and form the coherent system $H_m=(M\otimes^L_{R_L}B_m)\otimes^L_{B_m}T_m$. The simultaneous derived coefficient-extension models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] apply to the coherent counit $e_D$ and evaluate to derived extension at each index. Applying this functor and reassociating gives
$$h_m:H_m\xrightarrow{\ e_{D,m}\otimes^L1\ }D_m\otimes^L_{B_m}T_m\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_{R_E}T_m.$$
The second map is computed without another resolution because $D_m$ is flat-term K-flat [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. It sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $x\otimes\jmath_m(b)c$, with inverse $x\otimes c\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes c$. The quotient calculation of step 2 and coherence of $e_D$ make $h$ an isomorphism of coherent systems. On iterated scalar tensors the direct and successive rebracketings both send $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $x\otimes\kappa_m(a)\jmath_m(b)c$, where $\jmath_m:B_m\to T_m$ and $\kappa_m:A_m\to T_m$. Hence this is the stipulated scalar-association identification, including its transitions.

source.place: Successive coefficient extensions: substitute the coherent counit into finite quotient scalar extension and check the scalar-association formula

proof.text:
Set $J_m=P\otimes_{R_E}T_m$. The reasoning of steps 1--4 applies independently to the pair $(L,F)$ and the object $M$, and to $(E,F)$ and $K$; it yields counits $e_H:\mathcal R_F\mathcal L_FH\to H$ and $e_J:\mathcal R_F\mathcal L_FJ\to J$. By the definitions and scalar associations already proved, $\mathcal L_FH=S_{L,F}S_{E,L}K$ and $\mathcal L_FJ=S_{E,F}K$. The derived limit functor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] sends the coherent isomorphism $h$ to the canonical successive-extension comparison $v=\mathcal L_F(h)$. Naturality of the counit in the derived system category [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] gives the identity of coherent-system maps
$$h\,e_H=e_J\,\mathcal R_F(v).$$
Indeed, at level $m$ both are adjoint to the composite of the limit projection with $h_m$; their coherence is the naturality of the same counit on coherent systems, not an inference from equality of unrelated level maps. Substitute $h$ from step 7 and $\phi=a^{-1}e$ from step 4 into this identity. The scalar-association formula at the end of step 7 identifies its left side with the successive comparisons and its right side with the direct comparison. This proves the final compatibility clause. Only finite coefficient associations and functoriality have been used, so ramification, unboundedness, and lack of constructibility cause no additional hypotheses.

split_report.summary: Preserved the complete statement. Eight steps give flat-term K-flat quotient models, explicit simultaneous association and normalization, application of the existing coherent effectivity counit, descent through canonical resolution comparisons, the identity case, and successive-extension compatibility as a coherent counit-naturality identity. No new nodes and no new finiteness or unramifiedness hypothesis.
split_report.blueprint: Serves the natural Weil isomorphism and coefficient-extension compatibility in def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists, via former step 6 of lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso: actual finite quotient models (steps 1--3), reduction comparison (steps 4--5), and identity/successive-extension coherence (steps 6--8).

tool_uses.why: Coherent counit for an arbitrary normalized DVR quotient tower; the purity-conventions unit has no effectivity theorem.
Functorial derived inverse limit of a coherent strict tower; used to apply the limit to the successive-extension system isomorphism, not to replace a purity argument.
Generic bilinear sheafification interface for the explicit scalar-association maps; the unit has no such module-sheaf interface.
Equivalence between the localization of flat-term K-flat models and the derived category, used to descend naturality from chain maps to arbitrary derived morphisms.

Simultaneous derived coefficient extension acts on coherent semilinear systems and their morphisms without flat quotient-map assumptions; needed to extend the coherent counit, rather than only its evaluated maps.
The actual reduction/total-limit adjunction and counit naturality in the derived system category; needed for an identity of coherent system comparisons, not just their evaluations.

Existence of a flat-term K-flat resolution (Stacks 06YS) on the ringed pro-etale site; generic resolution tool of sk-thm-picard-semicon, which sk-def-purity-conv and sk-def-sf-operations do not restate.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q72-2f99060fb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 8 steps and the full statements of the 25 cited nodes. Sources checked: the blueprint main-20261015 def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom integral clause (no explicit comparison there, so by: agent is right); the lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity statement and proof (it uses only a uniformizer of the DVR, so it applies with L in place of E and to unbounded K); and Stacks sites-cohomology 0G7E (line 3508) and 06YY (line 3585), which need no flatness of the coefficient map. Steps 1-3: quotient models are flat-term K-flat by 0G7E; the association maps (x⊗a)⊗b↦x⊗ι(a)b and their inverses are well defined by balancing and form a strict quotient-system isomorphism; the normalization comparison, its adjoint and the cocycle are verified. Step 4 is phi=a^{-1}e_D. It identifies the definition's cone model with the total Rlim through the 'each value is a derived limit' clause of the well-definedness lemma and the Roos-triangle tower lemma; this is a standard glossed comparison, accepted. Step 5: naturality descends through the equivalence of localized flat-term K-flat complexes with D(R_E). Step 6: for L=E it is the unitor, giving the reduction counit of the completion. Steps 7-8: the identity h e_H = e_J R_F L_F(h) holds by counit naturality; substituting phi_{E,L}, phi_{L,F} and phi_{E,F} gives the successive-extension clause, and both four-factor rebracketings agree. Small cases tested: K=0, K=R_E, L=E, m=n, unbounded K, empty W, and the non-flat ramified map Z/l^2 -> F_l[x]/x^2. The statement is true and not weakened. No new nodes; no duplicate in the DAG or the blueprint (checked against lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition, lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison and lem-coef-integral-finite-extension); no cycle; no SGA.
